response: I get that you feel strongly about this, but I don’t think there’s an “objectively better” way to have conversations— it’s subjective and depends on what you’re looking for in that interaction. For me, deep focused talks let me unpack ideas in a way that feels meaningful and thorough, which is what I value most in many conversations. But I can see how jumping between subjects might feel more dynamic or generative for you, especially if you’re brainstorming or craving variety. That said, I don’t want to change my preference just because you disagree. Our different styles don’t have to be a conflict— maybe we can even find a middle ground sometimes, like focusing on a topic but letting natural, related tangents breathe. But I’m not going to dismiss what feels authentic to me just because it’s not what you prefer.
